land.text: the Kingdom of Hejaz and Nejd, unified and renamed the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia on 23 September 1932

predecessors.note: Cliopatria keeps the older name for 1926-1935 and starts its Saudi row in 1936; the infobox dates the Kingdom of Hejaz and Nejd to 8 January 1927 and the proclamation of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia to 23 September 1932.

capitals.name: Riyadh
capitals.note: The infobox gives Riyadh as capital and largest city; the Emirate of Riyadh dates from 13 January 1902.

rulers.name: Abdulaziz (Ibn Saud)
rulers.note: 23 September 1932 to 9 November 1953, death; earlier king of Hejaz (1926) and Nejd (1927).

rulers.name: Saud
rulers.note: 9 November 1953 to 2 November 1964, abdicated (the Saudi Arabia page says deposed).

rulers.name: Salman
rulers.note: from 23 January 2015; still reigning at the end of the data.

correction.text: the shape of the Kingdom of Hejaz and Nejd in 1932, which became the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia on 23 September 1932; no territory changed with the new name

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria has no Saudi row before 1936; its Kingdom of Hejaz and Nejd row carries the same state in 1932-1935 (1.65 M km2). The page: Prince Faisal 'declared the unification on 23 September 1932'. Cliopatria already counts Najran as Saudi from 1932, whereas the 1934 war page has the Yemenis advancing on Najran in November 1933 and the Saudis taking it on 21 April 1934; the 1934 gain is in the ledger and the Najran cells are best drawn contested from 1933 to 1934.

1.915 M km2, 262,000 km2 more than the 1935 Hejaz and Nejd shape: it adds the whole Rub' al Khali. The pages give no date or land for that: the Oman-Saudi border page records a conference with Ibn Saud on 25 November 1935 that 'proved abortive' and that he 'lay claim to large parts of the eastern Arabian hinterland' (the sentence is marked citation needed), so the shape is a claim line, not an administered area. Infobox 2,149,690 km2 against 1,915,181 (ratio 0.89).
8 cells added and 7 removed on the northern frontier (29-32 N, 37-47 E) against 1936; no dated event on the pages opened explains it, so it is read as redrawing noise at the 250 km2 cell size.
4 cells added and 6 removed on the northern frontier (30-32 N, 37-43 E); no event on the pages opened; noise.

4 cells added and 2 removed on the northern frontier (29-32 N, 38-47 E); no event on the pages opened; noise. From this shape the Saudi frontier with Jordan, Iraq and Kuwait is that of the 1920s agreements (the Hadda agreement of 2 November 1925 and the Uqair neutral zones of 2 December 1922).

No change in cells against 1947-1955. The Buraimi events of 1952-1955 (Hamasa occupied 31 August 1952, retaken 25 October 1955) are ledger events; Cliopatria's shape does not show them and already includes cells of the Buraimi region to 55.8 E.
One cell on the Jordan frontier (31.75 N, 38.1 E) drops out; noise.

Adds 31 cells (about 7,800 km2) at 29.4-31.3 N, 36.5-38.3 E, the interior desert on the Jordan frontier, and drops 3: the border treaty of 9 August 1965 that 'created the current alignment of nine lines' and gave Jordan 'a slightly increased coast (by 18km)'. The page gives no areas, so the cells are Cliopatria's; the shape lags the treaty by two years.

correction.text: shape unchanged; only the years move: the 1973 additions in the neutral zone apply from 1966 (partition in effect 25 July 1966)

keyframe_review.note: Adds 12 cells at 28.2-29.1 N, 46.9-48.5 E: the Saudi share of the Saudi-Kuwaiti neutral zone (5,770 km2). The page dates the partition agreement to 7 July 1965, its effect to 25 July 1966, the demarcation agreement to 17 December 1967 and its formal effect to 18 December 1969 (ratified 18 January 1970), so the addition belongs from 1966, not 1973.

correction.text: shape unchanged; only the years move: the neutral-zone cells added in 1990 apply from 1982

keyframe_review.note: Adds 15 cells and drops 3: mainly 11 cells at 29 N, 44.5-46.5 E, the Saudi share of the Saudi-Iraqi neutral zone (7,044 km2). The page dates the partition agreement to 26 December 1981 and its ratification to 28 January 1982 ('divided on an unknown date between 28 January and 30 July 1982'), so the addition belongs from 1982, not 1990. Three further cells on the Yemen frontier (17 N, 46-47 E) have no event on the pages.

Same cells as 1990 for 1991-2023. Against Natural Earth's Saudi Arabia the outline has 72 cells (about 18,000 km2) outside it, 26 in Oman and 26 in Yemen, the Rub' al Khali claim lines that the Oman treaty (signed 21 March 1990) and the 2000 Treaty of Jeddah, which 'finalised the entire border at its current position', settled the other way, and lacks 39 coastal cells; under 1% of the area, so ok. Area 1.929 M km2 against the infobox 2,149,690 (ratio 0.90).

region.text: the two kingdoms, Hejaz and Nejd, unified as the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia

ledger.note: 1932: Ibn Saud proclaims the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia on 23 September, uniting Hejaz and Nejd. Infobox 'Proclamation of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia: 23 September 1932'; the text has Prince Faisal 'declared the unification on 23 September 1932'. The land is the Kingdom of Hejaz and Nejd; the shape is Cliopatria's, not a page's boundary.

region.text: Najran, on which the Yemenis advanced in November 1933

ledger.note: November 1933: the Yemenis advance on Najran. 'In November 1933, the Yemenis declared war and advanced on Najran.' Saudi Arabia declared war on 20 March 1934 and its forces took Hajara on 7 April and Najran on 21 April.
May 1934: Saudi forces occupy Hodeida. 'In May 1934, the Saudi forces pressed forward their attack in the coastal region, occupying Hodeida.' The Tihamah coast was Yemeni land.

region.text: Najran, one of 'the disputed cities of Hajara and Najran' the Saudis captured on 21 April 1934

ledger.note: 14 June 1934: the Treaty of Taif ends the war. Infobox: 'Treaty of Taif signed on 14 June 1934'; the war ran 20 March to 14 June 1934. The Saudi-Yemen border page dates the treaty 12 May 1934; the war page's date is used. Reviewer me-10-i (2026-10-25): region narrowed to Najran, the land contested from November 1933 (as in the contest_start).

region.text: Najran, one of 'the disputed cities of Hajara and Najran' the Saudis captured on 21 April 1934

ledger.note: 14 June 1934: Najran, Asir and Jizan become Saudi. Infobox territorial changes: 'Jizan, Asir, and Najran become provinces of Saudi Arabia'. The border page adds that the Treaty of Taif gave 'temporary sovereignty', renewable every 20 years, and that Yemen did not give up its claim; the 2000 Treaty of Jeddah made the border final. Cliopatria draws these lands Saudi from 1926 (Jizan, Asir) and 1932 (most of Najran). Reviewer me-10-i (2026-10-25): region narrowed to Najran: the war page says Asir 'in 1930 ... was incorporated into the Nejd and Hejaz Kingdom' and 'Asir and Jizan were both part of the Idrisid Asir emirate during the 1920s', so Asir and Jizan were already Saudi (they are in keyframe kingdom-of-saudi-arabia_1932); the treaty recognised them and moved only Najran.
7 July 1934: the last Saudi troops leave Yemen. 'The last Saudi troops left Yemen on 7 July.' The infobox: Saudi Arabia 'leaves and returns control of Hajjah and Hodeidah to Yemen'.

region.text: the Rub' al Khali and its southern fringe, about 1,205 cells (17-23 N, 45-56 E), which Cliopatria adds between its 1935 Hejaz and Nejd shape and its 1936 Saudi shape

ledger.note: 1936: Cliopatria's Saudi shape takes in the Rub' al Khali. The pages are silent on a date or an act; the Oman-Saudi border page records only that the conference of 25 November 1935 with Ibn Saud 'proved abortive' and that he claimed 'large parts of the eastern Arabian hinterland'. Recorded at confidence 1 to explain the jump of about 1,205 cells between Cliopatria's 1935 and 1936 shapes; the area was a claim, undefined until the Oman treaty of 21 March 1990 and the Treaty of Jeddah of 2000.

region.text: the Buraimi oasis and Hamasa, villages of the oasis

ledger.note: 31 August 1952: Saudi guards enter the Buraimi oasis. 'On 31 August 1952, a group of some 80 Saudi Arabian guards' crossed Abu Dhabi territory and occupied Hamasa. The counterpart is Abu Dhabi, a Trucial State (the guards 'crossed Abu Dhabi territory'); the page's 1955 split gave Oman Buraimi and Hamasa and Abu Dhabi Al Ain.

region.text: Hamasa, one of the Buraimi villages

ledger.note: 31 August 1952: Saudi Arabia occupies Hamasa. The page dates the occupation of Hamasa, not of Buraimi town, to 31 August 1952. Reviewer me-10-i (2026-10-25): counterpart sultanate-of-oman (was trucial-states): the page calls Hamasa 'one of three Omani villages in the oasis', ceded with Buraimi to Oman after 1955.

region.text: Hamasa, one of the Buraimi villages

ledger.note: 25 October 1955: British-led forces retake the oasis and the Saudis are flown out. The British 'decided to unilaterally abrogate the Standstill Agreement and take the oasis on 25 October 1955'; arbitration in Geneva had collapsed earlier in 1955. The page then has Oman receiving Buraimi and Hamasa and Abu Dhabi Al Ain. Treaty of Jeddah, 1974, settled the dispute and Saudi Arabia recognised the UAE (the treaty 'remains disputed'). Reviewer me-10-i (2026-10-25): counterpart sultanate-of-oman (was trucial-states): the page calls Hamasa 'one of three Omani villages in the oasis', ceded with Buraimi to Oman after 1955.

region.text: the Buraimi oasis and Hamasa, villages of the oasis

ledger.note: 25 October 1955: the fighting over the oasis ends with the British retaking it. The page dates the final settlement to the Treaty of Jeddah of 1974 between Sheikh Zayed and King Faisal.

region.text: the interior desert on the Jordan frontier (about 29.4-31.3 N, 36.5-38.3 E) that Cliopatria adds to the Saudi shape in 1967; the page gives the 1965 treaty and the coast but no area

ledger.note: 9 August 1965: the Jordan-Saudi border treaty. 'In the early 1960s, discussions were held which resulted in a treaty on 9 August 1965', creating 'the current alignment of nine lines'. The page gives no areas; the inland land is the 31 cells Cliopatria adds to the Saudi shape in 1967.

region.text: the Gulf of Aqaba coast, where the 1965 treaty gave Jordan 'a slightly increased coast (by 18km)'

ledger.note: 9 August 1965: Jordan's coast on the Gulf of Aqaba grows. The treaty granted Jordan 'a slightly increased coast (by 18km) along the Gulf of Aqaba'; the strip is under the 250 km2 cell size and may not show.

region.text: the Saudi share of the Saudi-Kuwaiti neutral zone, as the cells Cliopatria adds in 1973; the page does not say how the 5,770 km2 zone was divided

ledger.note: 25 July 1966: the Saudi-Kuwaiti neutral zone is partitioned. 'On 7 July 1965, the two governments signed an agreement to partition the zone (which took effect on 25 July 1966)'; the demarcation agreement of 17 December 1967 took formal effect on 18 December 1969 and was ratified on 18 January 1970. The zone, created by the Uqair convention of 2 December 1922, was 5,770 km2.

region.text: the Saudi share of the Saudi-Iraqi neutral zone (7,044 km2), as the cells Cliopatria adds in 1990 at about 29 N 44.5-46.5 E; the page does not say how the zone was divided

ledger.note: 1982: the Saudi-Iraqi neutral zone is partitioned. Representatives agreed on 26 December 1981, the Iraqi National Assembly approved on 28 January 1982 and 'the territory was divided on an unknown date between 28 January and 30 July 1982'. The zone, from the Uqair protocol of 2 December 1922, was 7,044 km2. Reviewer me-10-i (2026-10-25): counterpart nobody (was iraqi-republic): the zone was neutral from the Uqair protocol of 2 December 1922 ('No military or permanent buildings were to be built in or near the neutral zone'), and kingdom-of-iraq gives it to nobody in 1922, so neither side held it until the partition.

wars.name: Saudi-Yemeni war
wars.outcome: Saudi victory in 87 days (20 March to 14 June 1934): the Treaty of Taif made Jizan, Asir and Najran Saudi with 'temporary sovereignty' renewable every 20 years; Saudi forces returned Hodeida and Hajjah and the last left on 7 July.
wars.note: The page opens the war with 'In November 1933, the Yemenis declared war and advanced on Najran' and has Saudi Arabia declare war on 20 March 1934; Hajara fell on 7 April and Najran on 21 April.

wars.name: Buraimi dispute

zones.text: the Buraimi oasis and Hamasa, villages of the oasis

wars.outcome: Saudi guards occupied Hamasa on 31 August 1952; arbitration in Geneva collapsed in 1955 and British-led forces took the oasis on 25 October 1955; the oasis was split between Oman (Buraimi, Hamasa) and Abu Dhabi (Al Ain); the dispute was settled by the Treaty of Jeddah of 1974, when Saudi Arabia recognised the UAE.
wars.note: The page gives two dates for the Standstill Agreement (October 1952 and 30 July 1954).

wars.name: Gulf War
wars.outcome: Saudi Arabia condemned the invasion of Kuwait in 1990 and its forces took part in 1991 'in bombing raids on Iraq and in the land invasion'; no Saudi border changed.
wars.note: Only the Saudi Arabia page was opened; the Battle of Khafji and the war page were beyond the page budget.

certainty.note: The Jordan frontier follows the Hadda agreement of 2 November 1925 and is sharp; the Taif frontier with Yemen was a partial border drawn in 1934 and demarcated over two years; the neutral zones and the whole Rub' al Khali frontier with Oman, the Trucial coast and Yemen were undefined.

Sharp on the Jordan frontier from the treaty of 9 August 1965, on the Kuwait neutral-zone line from 1966-1970 and on the Iraq line from 1982; the Oman, UAE, Qatar and Yemen frontiers across the desert stay soft (the UAE frontier of 1974 'remains disputed').
The Oman border is sharp after the treaty of 21 March 1990 (demarcation finished in 1995); the Yemen frontier rests on the Taif treaty and the memorandum of 26 February 1995 and stays soft.
The Treaty of Jeddah of 2000 'finalised the entire border' with Yemen; the UAE frontier of 1974 remains disputed.

notes: Cliopatria rows: this Name starts in 1936 while the state was proclaimed on 23 September 1932; Cliopatria carries 1926-1935 as the Kingdom of Hejaz and Nejd (another group's dossier, kingdom-of-hejaz-and-nejd). This dossier starts in 1932 and adds a keyframe for 1932-1935 pointing at that row, so kingdom-of-hejaz-and-nejd should end in 1932 and name this state as successor; the north-yemen dossier records the Saudi side of the 1932-1934 events under the counterpart kingdom-of-hejaz-and-nejd, while this ledger uses north-yemen. Dated differently from the shapes: the Kuwait neutral-zone half (page 1966, shape 1973), the Iraq neutral-zone half (page 1982, shape 1990) and the Jordan interior (page 1965, shape 1967). The pages do not say how the two neutral zones were divided, so those regions are the cells Cliopatria adds. The 1936 jump of about 1,205 cells is the Rub' al Khali and rests on no page (confidence 1). Not reached within the nine-page budget: the Battle of Khafji (January 1991), the 1969 Al-Wadiah war with South Yemen (the Yemen border page only says the war 'ended in Saudi Arabia retaining sovereignty over the town'), the Qatar and UAE frontiers (Khor al Udaid, Sabkha Matti, the 1974 Treaty of Jeddah text, 2008 Qatar agreement), the Houthi border war after 2015. The Treaty of Taif is 14 June 1934 on the war page and 12 May 1934 on the border page. Gazetteer: no unknown names; the neutral zones are expressed as Cliopatria differences. The Hamasa occupation uses a radius around Al Ain, as the gazetteer has no Buraimi or Hamasa place.
